Hi team,

We received a SIG/CAIQ intake from Helix Health (compliance@helixhealth.org) requesting access-control evidence to close out a SOC2 readiness review. They specifically want:

- A one-week anonymized sample of SSO session logs (SAML assertions + timestamp, user_id hash, session_id)
- SCIM delta export covering role assignments and user provisioning for the past 90 days
- RBAC matrix (roles -> permissions) and a short changelog highlighting any privilege reductions in the last 6 months (least-privilege proof-of-change)
- List of service accounts and justification for any with >write privileges

I've attached the intake email from their auditor. Can we confirm scope and owners: Irene, can you own SCIM export + redaction? Sean, can you own RBAC matrix + changelog? I'll coordinate the SSO sampling and package everything for a secure share.

Target ship: EOD Friday (2027-06-11). If anything blocks that timeline, surface it here.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz

Vanessa,

Thanks — I can take point on the SCIM export. A couple clarifying questions before I start pulling data:

1) Retention window: you asked for "past 90 days" — do we want to include tombstoned users (soft-deletes) or only active provisioning events?
2) Service accounts: do we have a designation list for which accounts are considered machine/service vs human? I can cross-reference the service-account tag but want to avoid manual churn.
3) Format: will a JSONL delta with schema and a short readme be acceptable to the auditor, or do they prefer CSV?

I'll prepare a redaction checklist (PII removal, email hashing) and run a quick sampling job. If Sean can drop the RBAC matrix template you want me to align with, I'll map SCIM attributes to role ids.

Vanessa —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A few notes from our side to ensure the package is consumable:

- SSO sample: a 7-day window is fine. Please include SAML Subject NameID (hashed), assertion issue/invalidate timestamps, and an indicator of authn_context (mfa/no-mfa). CSV is preferred for the sample for easier ingestion, with a short README describing the hashing method.
- SCIM delta: JSONL is preferred for the delta snapshots; include an exported schema file (we use urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User mapping).
- RBAC matrix: an XLSX with separate tabs for "roles", "role_permissions", and "recent_changes" is ideal. In the recent_changes tab, note the ticket/reference for each change and the rationale (e.g., privilege reduction).
- Service accounts: we need a short justification document for any service account with outsized privileges; a line item per account is fine.

I've attached the SIG control checklist (SIG_v2026_controls.pdf) with the specific controls the Helix team flagged regarding provisioning and access reviews. Also: is there an internal owner who can sign the attestation for least-privilege changes?

If you can upload to a secure Share with an access expiration URL (or send via DocuSign if attestation is needed), that will work.

Best,
Priya R.
Auditor, Auditsuite
priya@auditsuite.com
